title: 8 AWG stranded copper THHN/THWN-2 building wire

sources.citation: Typical published construction of 8 AWG THHN/THWN-2 (a US maker's public specification sheet, revised 02/2026, read; it carries no ampacity column; listed to UL 83, cited by number): made 19-strand from 8 AWG to 4/0; this size has a 30 mil PVC wall (0.762 mm) under a 5 mil nylon covering (0.127 mm), rounded from mils; colour-coded black, white, red, blue, green, yellow, orange, brown, grey, purple and pink (the sheet's tan has no colour id), most colours on all sizes. Rated 90 °C dry (THHN) and wet (THWN-2): the pinned insulation row thhnThwn2. Paraphrased; no table copied. The outer diameter is derived, never stored.

Soft (annealed) uncoated copper, as public THHN/THWN-2 and MTW sheets state for the conductor (concentric-stranded per ASTM B8; the standards cited by number, not read). Its resistivity, temperature coefficient and density are the pinned materials row copperAnnealed (100 % IACS, NBS Handbook 100). The area comes from the AWG definition (AWG_GAUGES), never from a conductor table.

A stranded conductor's resistance is its nominal area's times a lay factor of 1.02 for concentric Class B/C stranding up to 4/0 (NBS Handbook 100, Copper Wire Tables, 1966, its stranded-conductor tables and appendix; NBS Handbook 109, Aluminum Wire Tables, 1972, its twist factor of 1.02; both read in full in the P3 source pre-audit): the helical strands are longer than the conductor. Paraphrased; no table reproduced.
